scenes.keyframe_visual: Anu pushes through the glass lobby door, tote crossbody, phone pinned to her shoulder, ID card swiping at the turnstile
scenes.camera: handheld follow, walking backward ahead of her

dialogue.voice: young Indian woman, early 20s, quick Mumbai English, slightly breathless when nervous

dialogue.line: He fixed one comma. My whole evening, gone.
dialogue.voice: young Indian woman, early 20s, quick Mumbai English, slightly breathless when nervous

scenes.micro_acting: ID card beeps red first try, she swipes again without looking, phone still at her ear

scenes.location: Meridian lobby turnstile to elevator bank
scenes.keyframe_visual: Anu crossing the lobby floor past the security guard, phone screen glowing with a live recording waveform as elevator doors open
scenes.camera: locked wide then macro insert on her thumb, rack focus to the opening doors

dialogue.line: Honestly, he's just lonely. Glasses don't help.

young Indian woman, early 20s, quick Mumbai English, slightly breathless when nervous

scenes.location: Meridian open-plan floor toward Vikram's cabin
scenes.keyframe_visual: Priya stapling client folders at her desk, stapler jamming loudly, Anu weaving past her toward the glass cabin, lanyard trembling
scenes.camera: static close on Priya then handheld follow onto Anu approaching the cabin

dialogue.line: Stapler's jammed again. Use mine, it's by the printer.

dialogue.line: Vikram sir called me. I have to go.

scenes.keyframe_visual: Vikram seated behind a clean desk, a photo frame lying face-down beside his laptop, Anu seated across from him, a white envelope on the desk between them
scenes.camera: static medium through the glass wall, slow push in on her face

dialogue.line: 'Just lonely,' you said. Accurate, at least.
dialogue.voice: middle-aged Indian man, low measured baritone, precise English, long pauses

dialogue.line: Sir, I'll resign. Please don't call HR.
dialogue.voice: young Indian woman, early 20s, quick Mumbai English, slightly breathless when nervous

dialogue.line: Take it. Two thousand. You told me the truth when lying was easier.
dialogue.voice: middle-aged Indian man, low measured baritone, precise English, long pauses

scenes.micro_acting: he taps the face-down frame once, doesn't flip it, her hand hovers over the envelope without touching it
scenes.narrative_job: plant the face-down photo, reversal - cash instead of firing, the deal begins

scenes.location: Meridian stairwell down to the chai stall
scenes.keyframe_visual: Anu walking past Priya's desk toward the glass doors downstairs, envelope folded small inside her tote, glancing back once at the cabin
scenes.camera: static wide, she shrinks toward the glass doors and the frame edge

dialogue.line: Okay. Okay, it's just paper. It's just an envelope.
dialogue.voice: young Indian woman, early 20s, quick Mumbai English, slightly breathless when nervous

scenes.micro_acting: she mutters to herself, fingers the envelope's fold, pushes the glass door open
scenes.narrative_job: cliffhanger - value turn from safe to exposed, decision unresolved

new_facts.fact: Anu's voice note criticizing Vikram ('lonely tyrant') auto-sent to Vikram instead of Priya
Vikram paid Anu Rs 2,000 cash in a white envelope for her honesty instead of firing her
Vikram keeps a photo frame face-down on his desk which he does not explain
